scope: Independent static inspection and AST syntax checks of the exact combined recipe-extension and finite CPU worker code. No Colab execution, Drive call, runtime database change, training or model weight loading was performed by this reviewer.
syntax: Both Python files parsed successfully with ast.parse
bounded_fixes_applied_with_parent_author: Combined cell now checks for an existing active audit thread before extend_recipe can mutate the SQLite recipe identity; the second guard remains before checkpoint creation.
SQLite snapshot backup target closes explicitly in a finally block; a sqlite3 connection context alone does not close a connection.
Per-thread Drive client, reader and payload-cache initialization now occur inside the protected try block, so setup errors record STOPPED status and execute final status persistence.
current_member is recorded before cache access and consume, so a failing member is correctly identified rather than showing the prior successful member.
root_prior_changes_verified: Unnecessary probe audit connection is absent.
Initial old-recipe report is labeled source_migration_report. The active new-recipe report is populated from the new FullArchiveAudit before the first snapshot save.
static_checks: Recipe bytes are explicitly SHA-pinned before JSON decoding. Existing V3.extend_recipe validates immutable source/chat prefixes and original DB identity; the combined cell calls it before replacing recipe_all and V3_ID.

The worker asserts218 source members plus31 chat members, matching the249-member new recipe. FullArchiveAudit.next_entry controls finite order, and FullArchiveAudit.consume enforces source-first processing and exact row count at EOF.

Checkpoint lookup searches the existing target folder for the exact V3 recipe identity and refuses an existing match instead of creating a duplicate. New checkpoint identity remains distinct from the preserved V2 parent.
A new checkpoint is created with UNINITIALIZED hash. The worker saves a complete SQLite backup and verifies every remote raw byte/hash before setting RUNNING_DATA_ONLY and entering its consume loop.

Each save checks writer_session, recipe identity and last expected data_sha256, uploads to the same checkpoint ID, then updates both closure checkpoint and global v3_ref. This resolves the prior stale-reference problem.
The completed upload metadata is retained if readback fails, but no new verified proof or latest_checkpoint_ref is written until full raw size/hash and post-write writer checks succeed.

A processing exception records STOPPED_REQUIRES_AUDIT_REPAIR, the actual report, and one checkpoint-save attempt. Save errors are recorded separately; finalization closes the auditor and writes status.

The finite loop stops at next_entry=None. A zero-row EOF confirmation is allowed only when complete/already_complete is explicit. A no-progress span without completion raises instead of looping forever.

Final checkpoint save precedes the final report. The report's clean-complete flag selects AUDIT_PASS_PENDING_CURRICULUM_ACCEPTANCE; retained findings select AUDIT_FINISHED_WITH_FINDINGS. No branch declares training ready or starts training.
Unknown regression_only finding and protected-source policies are not changed by this worker code. Existing source/hash/split findings remain under the auditor.
deployment_limits: Thread guards only cover the observed kernel. Drive metadata get-then-update is an optimistic check, not an atomic distributed lock. This limitation is explicitly disclosed in both code and status.

Parent must verify the intended live runtime and no other active writer before deployment. Re-running a cell that finds an existing checkpoint intentionally stops for exact-ID/hash resume; it must not be bypassed to create a copy.
Actual cloud progress, initial/final checkpoint readbacks and worker state must be read after deployment. This static PASS does not claim a successful cloud launch or completed249-member audit.
A Colab kernel can terminate; only the last whole-raw-verified saved checkpoint is durable. A later local cursor is not a cloud durability claim.
